xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2684: refactor(dashboard): redesign Tiered Execution settings — routing ladder, overrides-only kinds, advanced disclosures, restore compaction_reroute

plan.title: refactor(dashboard): redesign Tiered Execution settings — routing ladder, overrides-only kinds, advanced disclosures, restore compaction_reroute
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

narratives.Problem: Settings → Tiered Execution (TieredExecutionSection.tsx, 851 lines) edits the difficulty→tier total function as N:M per-tier checkboxes (invalid states reachable, errors surface far from the cause), renders tiers as unordered look-alike cards with no cost signal, shows nine kind selects even when nothing is overridden, gives full cards to all-default Feed/Escalation/Replay, has NO control for compaction_reroute despite it being in the schema, defaults, live config, and docs, and silently accepts harness/provider mismatches (the PAN-1865 CLIProxy trap).
narratives.Proposal: Rebuild the panel per the BINDING operator-approved mockup v2: crews replace tier names entirely on the operator surface. A pure mapping module (tiered-crews.ts) converts TieredExecutionConfig ⇄ crews (identical staffing merges on import per D-2; tier names derived from owned difficulties on save per D-3; by_kind rewritten in the same save). The board makes difficulty→crew assignment a total function (coverage errors unrepresentable). Crew rows expand to single-model or weighted-mix editors with a PAN-1865 warning chip and harness-auto form state (file keeps concrete harness, D-4). Supervisor, kind overrides (overrides-only), Commit feed, Escalation, Session replay (adds the missing compaction_reroute select), and a YAML preview render as collapsed disclosures with plain-language resolution summaries. A no-loss inventory test gates deletion of the old render. Server-side schema, validation, and runtime resolution are untouched (D-1/NFR-1).
narratives.NonGoals:
- No server/schema/runtime changes: src/lib/settings-api-tiered-execution.ts, src/lib/agents/tier-table.ts, and all resolution paths stay byte-identical (NFR-1)
- Do NOT ship the mockup's 'Preview a state' scenario buttons — they are mockup-only pedagogy (D-9)
- No merge-on-save dedup of identical crews; identical crews serialize as two tiers and merge on next load (D-8)
- No 'auto' value stored in config: harness in the file is always a concrete Harness value; auto is a form state only (D-4)
- No per-issue tiered-execution override UI (PAN-2383 — tracked separately as PAN-2683)
- No new dependencies; no YAML library — the preview uses a ~30-line local serializer (NFR-4, D-10)
- No new Mintlify user-facing page: configuration/*.mdx has no tiered-execution page today (verified 2026-07-14 in the PRD), so only docs/TIERED-EXECUTION.md is updated
- No change to TieredExecutionSection props, DEFAULT_MODEL/DEFAULT_SUPERVISOR_MODEL exports, or the SettingsPage.tsx:549 mount (NFR-2)

autoDecisions.summary: Pre-resolved the D-4 implementation checkpoint: provider_harnesses exists on the frontend SettingsConfig at src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/Settings/types.ts:45 (Partial<Record<Provider, HarnessOverride>>); providerDefaultHarness() reads it and falls back to the built-in table (anthropic→claude-code, openai→codex, else→ohmypi) mirroring getBuiltInDefaultHarness in src/lib/providers.ts:249.
autoDecisions.rationale: The PRD marked this as an implementation checkpoint with a stated fallback; verifying it at planning time removes a judgment call from the work agent.

autoDecisions.summary: Split PRD work item 4 into two vBRIEF items: supervisor + kind overrides (FR-4/FR-5) and advanced disclosures + YAML preview (FR-6/FR-7).
autoDecisions.rationale: They are independent FR groups with separately testable acceptance criteria; smaller diffs review better and the task-granularity rule says split when the title needs 'and' across unrelated surfaces.

autoDecisions.summary: Items 2–6 are serialized (readiness: sequential) rather than parallel-dispatchable.
autoDecisions.rationale: They all rebuild the same file (TieredExecutionSection.tsx) incrementally; parallel dispatch would conflict on every edit. Item 1 (pure module) is the only independently dispatchable foundation.

items.title: Pure crews mapping module: TieredExecutionConfig ⇄ crews (tiered-crews.ts) with unit tests

metadata.parallelSafeReason: New standalone pure module plus its own new test file; it touches no existing files, so it cannot conflict with any other work.
expected_outputs: tiered-crews.test.ts passes with all cases green

narrative.Action: Create src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/Settings/sections/tiered-crews.ts — pure functions only, no React, no new dependencies. Exports: importCrews(config) → { crews, assign, rest } grouping tiers with identical staffing into one crew per D-2 (single: same model+harness; mix: same {model, harness, weight} triples after sorting entries by model id) owning the union of their difficulties; serializeCrews(crews, assign, rest) → TieredExecutionConfig writing derived tier names per D-3 (owned difficulties in ladder order trivial→expert joined with '-'), preserving the PAN-2391 representative entry rule (top-level model/harness mirror the max-weight distribution entry), and rewriting by_kind values to derived names in the same save; deriveTierName(diffs); crewLabel(crew) ('Kimi K2.7 Code' for single, '4-model mix' style for mixes); blendedCost(crew, catalog) using costPer1MTokens from MODELS_BY_PROVIDER (modelCatalog.ts:14) — weight-blended over entries that have a cost, null when none do (render as '—', never $0); providerDefaultHarness(modelId, settings) reading settings provider_harnesses (types.ts:45) with the built-in fallback table (anthropic→claude-code, openai→codex, else→ohmypi; comment names src/lib/providers.ts getBuiltInDefaultHarness as source); renderYamlPreview(config) — ~30-line local serializer for the tiered_execution object, no YAML lib (D-10). Read rule: consume config.by_kind ?? config.byKind (both exist in types.ts) but always write the canonical by_kind key. Write __tests__/tiered-crews.test.ts with a fixture matching the operator's live shape: kimi solo tier + two identical 4-entry mix tiers → 2 crews.

items.title: Given the live-config fixture (kimi solo + two identical 4-entry mixes over medium/complex/expert), importCrews returns exactly 2 crews, the merged crew owning the union of the two tiers' difficulties

serializeCrews(importCrews(x)) round-trip preserves semantics: derived names correct for single ('medium'), contiguous ('trivial-simple'), and non-contiguous ('trivial-expert') ownership; representative entry preserved; by_kind values rewritten to derived names
blendedCost returns the weight-blended average over entries that carry costPer1MTokens and returns null (rendered '—', never $0) when no entry has a cost
providerDefaultHarness resolves from provider_harnesses when present on the settings payload and falls back to anthropic→claude-code / openai→codex / else→ohmypi when absent
renderYamlPreview produces the exact tiered_execution object the next save would send for a fixture config, with no YAML dependency added to package.json
Board (five difficulty columns, total-function crew assignment) + header row with state chip

expected_outputs: TieredExecutionSection.test.tsx passes including the untouched never-frontier test

narrative.Action: Rebuild TieredExecutionSection.tsx in place (keep the file, the props formData/saveErrorMessage/saveStatus/onSettingsChange, and the DEFAULT_MODEL/DEFAULT_SUPERVISOR_MODEL exports per NFR-2). Replace the difficulty-routing readout box and all per-tier difficulty checkboxes with the board: five difficulty columns (trivial→expert, mockup subtitles verbatim per D-9), each with a crew select listing existing crews by crewLabel plus '+ new crew…', a staffing summary, cost chip (cyan = money only), and crew-colored top border. '+ new crew…' creates a claude-haiku-4-5 single-model crew (never-frontier default) and opens its editor. Add the header row: title, plain-language explainer including the per-issue override chain sentence, state chip (Off / On · valid / Invalid — <reason>), enable switch. Delete inputDifficultyMap and the difficulty-coverage branches of validationReason (unrepresentable now); keep the mix-total and supervisor-required client checks and the existing serverTieredError derivation (TieredExecutionSection.tsx:182-195) routing into the red chip state per D-6. State uses crews from importCrews; all writes go through onSettingsChange with serializeCrews output — never a direct fetch.

items.title: The board renders exactly five difficulty columns with mockup subtitle copy, and changing a column's crew select emits the reassigned config through onSettingsChange
No UI path produces an unmapped or double-mapped difficulty: each column is a required single select and no difficulty checkbox surface remains in the rendered panel
'+ new crew…' creates a claude-haiku-4-5 single-model crew and opens its editor; the pre-existing never-frontier test (asserting DEFAULT_MODEL/DEFAULT_SUPERVISOR_MODEL) passes without modification
The header state chip renders 'Off' when disabled, 'On · valid' when clean, and a red 'Invalid — <reason>' for a mix totaling ≠100% and for a server saveErrorMessage
Crew roster rows with expandable single-model and weighted-mix editors, PAN-1865 chip, remove guard

expected_outputs: crew-row tests pass: warning chip, remove guard, representative rule, total-100 error

narrative.Action: Implement 'The crews' list: one expandable row per crew showing color dot, composition label (crewLabel), mix summary, amber PAN-1865 warning chip when the stored harness differs from providerDefaultHarness (D-4), owned-difficulties line ('handles trivial · simple' / 'handles nothing — assign it on the board or remove it'), and cost chip. Expanded: single-model editor (model select + harness select whose first option is 'auto (<provider default>)' — picking auto writes the provider default concrete value at save time) or mix editor (weighted bar, per-entry model/harness/weight/remove rows, running total with red state when ≠100, 'Add model'), plus 'Use one model'/'Use a weighted mix' toggle applying the representative rule on collapse (max-weight entry becomes top-level model/harness), and 'Remove crew' blocked with an explanatory message while the crew owns any difficulty. Re-express today's handleDistributionPatch/Add/Remove/Toggle semantics (TieredExecutionSection.tsx:285-320) over crew state. Extract a sibling CrewRow.tsx only if TieredExecutionSection.tsx exceeds ~500 lines. Rows and disclosure headers keyboard-operable: Enter/Space toggles, visible focus state (NFR-5). Two identical crews may coexist while editing — no live dedup (D-8).

items.title: Given a crew with kimi model and stored harness claude-code, the amber PAN-1865 chip renders ('⚠ harness overrides provider default — PAN-1865') and disappears when the harness select is set to auto
'Remove crew' on a crew owning difficulties renders an explanatory blocked message and does not mutate config; on a crew owning none it removes the crew from the outgoing config
Toggling mix→single applies the representative rule: the max-weight entry's model/harness become the crew's single staffing in the emitted config
The mix editor renders per-entry model/harness/weight/remove plus 'Add model', and a weights total ≠100 renders the inline red total error and flips the header chip to Invalid
When focused, a crew row header toggles expansion via Enter and via Space and renders a visible focus state
Supervisor sentence disclosure + overrides-only kind overrides with chips

expected_outputs: supervisor and kind-override tests pass (chips render only overrides; derived names serialized)

narrative.Action: Supervisor (FR-4): a disclosure whose collapsed summary is a sentence built from current state ('Standing reviewer — reviews every commit · Claude Sonnet 5 · owns inspection' style, mockup copy verbatim per D-9); expanded controls: model select, harness select (with auto option per D-4), subscribe select with the mockup's plain-language option labels, owns-inspection switch. Supervisor-required-when-tiers-exist stays server-enforced; keep the existing client check surfaced through the header chip. Kind overrides (FR-5): overrides-only rendering — default line 'All kinds follow difficulty routing.' (or 'N kinds overridden; …' when any exist), one chip per actual override with an ✕ that clears it, and an add row with kind + crew pickers and an 'Add override' button. Serialization writes by_kind with derived tier names via serializeCrews (reads by_kind ?? byKind, writes by_kind). The nine always-rendered selects are deleted in this item's diff (their write path is replaced by the chip UI; the no-loss test in no-loss-audit still asserts all 9 kinds remain available through the add-override picker).

Advanced disclosures: Commit feed, Escalation, Session replay (+ compaction_reroute), YAML preview

expected_outputs: disclosure tests pass including compaction_reroute round-trip under fake timers

narrative.Action: Implement the Advanced group as disclosures with one-line resolution summaries (mockup copy verbatim per D-9; e.g. escalation off → 'off — failures never change crews'). Commit feed: keep callouts select, max_diff_bytes, exclude and exclude_subjects CSV fields with the existing csvToList/listToCsv parsing and { debounce: true } save options. Escalation: keep enabled, retries_at_tier, max_promotions, and the flounder_budget_minutes five-input grid with current parse behavior. Session replay: keep replay_threshold and ADD the compaction_reroute select (D-7, restores the missing control): options rendered as the mockup's plain-language sentences ('bring back the same session as before' = off / 're-plan remaining work; retire crews no longer needed' = on); do NOT ship the mockup's 'new — in config, missing from today's UI' annotation tag. YAML preview (FR-7/D-10): a 'What this writes to config.yaml' disclosure rendering renderYamlPreview of the exact outgoing config; its collapsed summary lists the derived tier names. Debounce-related tests use vi.useFakeTimers() + advanceTimersByTimeAsync per the repo fake-timers rule.
